# read_B — pp. 39–41 (leaves n40–n42), established from the images

Line counts: p. 39 has five lines (leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔), p. 40 has five lines, p. 41 has five lines (leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔).
The witness's line breaks match the print on all three pages (15/15 lines).
Each line was cropped in quarters at ×3 and in 300-px strips at ×5. Every doubtful syllable was checked at ×7–×16, with letters of known value from the same page set beside it.
The scan is effectively bilevel and the letters are about 12–15 px wide. Two consequences:
- In this cutting, final ད and ང have almost the same outline at this resolution (compared side by side: ང of འོང/ངོ 39.3 and ཡང 41.4; ད of འོད 39.3 and དག 41.4). Where only that difference is at issue, the image cannot decide (see [?]).
- 39.2 is a crowded line (…སེམས་དཔའ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་ཀྱི་ཐུགས་ཀ་ནས… and …མདུན་དུ་མིག་གིས་མི་བཟོད་པ་ཙམ་དུ…). Many of its tshegs are fused into the head-line, so they can be neither seen nor ruled out. The letters agree with the witness throughout, so the witness's tshegs are kept there.

| page.line | witness → print | why |
|---|---|---|
| 39.1 | ཕྱུང་པོ → ཕུང་པོ | ×8: there is only the zhabs-kyu hook under ཕ, with no ya-btags |
| 39.3 | འོད་དུང་ཁ → འོད་དུད[?]་ཁ | ×8–×12: three letters between the tshegs (ད, then ད with zhabs-kyu, then a final). The final is ད or ང, which can't be told apart (see above). It is read དུད for the sense ("smoke-coloured"), following the other recension's དུད་ཀ. The witness's དུང ("conch") makes no sense of the dull hell-light |

## [?] (3)

- 39.3 དུད[?]: see the table. The third letter is certain, but its ད/ང identity is not.
- 39.4 དུ[?] (དམྱལ་བའི་འོད་དུ[?]་ཁ): the block is damaged here (broken strokes, ×12). The space from འོ to ཁ is 106 px. That is the same as 40.3 འོད་དུ་ཁ (104 px) and less than 39.3 འོད་དུད་ཁ (122 px), so there are two letters, not three. Witness དུ taken.
- 41.4 འཕྲང[?]: see the table.

## Witness readings checked and confirmed, though odd

- 39.1 and 41.2 ལ་མཚེར་བ: the letter before ཚེ has the closed loop of མ (×12). At 39.5 the print has ལ་འཚེར་བ, with a clear འ. See misprints.
- 39.2 ཡབ་ཡུམ་ཀྱི: ཀྱི after མ. It has the same outline at ×10 as the certain ཀྱི of གཟུགས་ཀྱི in 39.1. The other recension has གྱི. See misprints.
- 39.3 གཤིབས་མར: the ས is there (×8).
- 39.4 བཀྲག་མདངས, ཁྱོད་འཇིགས་པ (the print adds ཁྱོད).
- 40.3 བསུ་བ་ལ་ཡོངས་པ: ཡོངས with ས (see misprints).
- 40.3 འོད་དུ་ཁ: only two letters, ད and དུ (×7–×9), with no second final.
- 40.4 སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ཀྱི་བསུ་བའི: ཀྱི with no ས (×7). The next letter is the square བ.
- 40.5 སྲན་མི་བཟོད, དུས་མ་འབྱུང (མ, no vowel: the cross above it is a descender from 40.4), ལམ་དགག་པའི (ད + ག + ག, ×7).
- 41.3 སེམས་དཔས་ལམ (×6), 41.4 བསྐྱོར, 41.5 ས་རུ (zhabs-kyu under ར, ×7), བཏབ་པས། with a shad, not ༔ (×7).
- Line-end tshegs (in the order of the lines in read_B.txt):
  - present: 39.1 གཅིག་, 39.3 འོད་, 39.4 དེ་, 39.5 པར་, 40.3 ཁ་, 40.4 ནི་, 41.2 ཀྱཻ་, 41.3 ལམ་, 41.4 པའི་, 41.5 ཐུགས་
  - absent: 40.2 and 41.1 (see the table)
  - close calls: 39.2 བའི་ and 40.1 ཟེར་ are followed by filler dots, and the tsheg can't be told from the first dot. 40.5 པའི་ has only a small separate dot under the gi-gu tail. In all three the witness's tsheg is kept.

Not transcribed:
- Filler dots at line ends.
- Filler-like dots inside lines: 39.3 after ཁ (two dots at head-line height, after its tsheg); 40.5 after དེ་ནི (an extended head-stroke and two dots before ཐར); 41.5 after རྡོ་རྗེ (two dots before སེམས). These look like spacing fillers, not text.
- After ཡེ in 39.1, 40.1 and 41.3 there is a tsheg with a second, lower speck under it (ཡེ:ཤེས). This is taken as an ordinary tsheg.

## Fixes needed (`# fix:` lines)

```
# fix: དེ་ལམ་འཇིགས => དེ་ལ་མ་འཇིགས
# fix: དོའིའཕྲང => དོའི་འཕྲང
# fix: གསལལ་མཚེར => གསལ་ལ་མཚེར
```
- 39.5 ལམ (mid-line): ལ and མ have no tsheg between them, a contraction of ལ་མ ("do not fear it"). The witness also has ལམ.
- 40.2→40.3: no tsheg after དོའི at the line end (the next line starts with འཕྲང).
- 41.1→41.2: no tsheg after གསལ at the line end (the next line starts with ལ་མཚེར). If misprint 1 below is taken, the right side becomes གསལ་ལ་འཚེར.

There are no line-end abbreviations (པའཾ, ལཾ, ྶ) or contractions of the ནམཁའ kind on these pages.

## Suspected misprints (kept as printed)

1. 39.1 and 41.2 ལ་མཚེར་བ → ལ་འཚེར་བ ("glittering"). Certainty is moderate to high. མཚེར is not a word. The print itself writes དཀར་ལ་འཚེར་བ at 39.5, and the other recension has འཚེར at both places. Because it happens twice it could be the carver's habit. Proposed: `# fix: ལ་མཚེར => ལ་འཚེར` (both places). This is the drafter's choice.
2. 39.4 and 40.3 འོད་དུ་ཁ → འོད་དུད་ཁ ("the dull smoke-coloured light of hell"). Certainty is moderate to high. 39.3 has the full དུད (read with [?] for its final), and the other recension has དུད་ཀ throughout. དུ་ཁ makes no sense. Proposed: `# fix: འོད་དུ་ཁ => འོད་དུད་ཁ` (two places).
3. 40.3 བསུ་བ་ལ་ཡོངས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ → ཡོང་པ ("has come to meet you"). Certainty is high for the stem: ཡོངས ("all") makes no sense, and the other recension has བསུ་བ་འོང་བ. Proposed: `# fix: ལ་ཡོངས་པ => ལ་ཡོང་པ`. The print's པ/བ is left alone.
4. 39.2 ཡབ་ཡུམ་ཀྱི → གྱི (the genitive after མ). Certainty is moderate. The letter is certainly ཀ, and the other recension has གྱི. Possible `# fix: ཡུམ་ཀྱི་ཐུགས => ཡུམ་གྱི་ཐུགས`. This is the drafter's choice.
5. 40.5 ཐར་པའི་དུས་མ་འབྱུང་གིས༔ ("the time of liberation will not come"). The future needs མི, and the other recension has མི་འབྱུང་གི. Certainty is moderate. It can't be corrected in only one way: མ→མི, and also གིས→གི. Note only.
6. 40.4 སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ཀྱི་བསུ་བའི་ལམ: the other recension has ཀྱིས་བསུ་མའི. The genitive reads "the welcoming path of the obscurations", which is acceptable. Note only.

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: 40.2 སྙམ་བའི; 39.3 གཤིབས་མར (other recension གཤིབ); 40.5 སྲན (other recension བསྲན); 41.4 བསྐྱོར (other recension སྐྱོར); 41.5 བཏབ་པས། with a shad.

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

- 39.1: print …གནས་སུ་དག་པ༔ འོད་དཀར་པོ (a statement); other recension དག་པའི་འོད་དཀར་པོ ("the white light which is the purified aggregate…").
- 39.2: print མིག་གིས་མི་བཟོད་པ; other recension མིག་གིས་ལྟ་མི་བཟོད་པ. Same sense. Print ཐུགས་ཀ་ནས་ཁྱོད (no ༔).
- 39.4: print བཀྲག་མདངས་དང་ལྡན་པ…ཁྱོད་འཇིགས་པ; other recension བཀྲག་དང་ལྡན་པ…འཇིགས་པ. Same sense.
- 39.5: print འོད་དཀར་པོ་དཀར་ལ་འཚེར་བ ("white and glittering"); other recension བཀྲག་ལ་འཚེར་བ ("lustrous and glittering").
- 40.1: print རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐུགས་རྗེའི་འོད་ཟེར ("rays of compassion"); other recension ཐུགས་ཀའི་འོད་ཟེར ("rays from the heart").
- 40.2–3: print དེ་ནས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་ཁྱོད་བར་དོའི་འཕྲང་ལ་བསུ་བ་ལ་ཡོངས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ ("then the Blessed One Vajrasattva, father-mother, has come to meet you in the narrow passage of the between"). Other recension དེ་ནི་…རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཁྱོད་བར་དོའི་འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ལ་བསུ་བ་འོང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ ("that is Vajrasattva coming to meet you in the terrors of the between"). The print adds ཡབ་ཡུམ and has འཕྲང for འཇིགས་སྐྲག.
- 40.4: print དེ་ལ་ཆགས་ན་ནི; other recension ཆགས་ན་ཁྱོད. Same sense.
- 40.5: print ཐར་པའི་དུས ("the time of liberation"); other recension ཐོན་པའི་དུས ("the time of getting out"). Print དེ་ནི་ཐར་པའི་ལམ་དགག; other recension དེ་ཐར་བའི་ལམ་དགག. Same.
- 41.1: print མིག་མ་བལྟ་བར; other recension དེ་ལ་མིག་གིས་མ་ལྟ་བར. Same sense.
- 41.2: print མོས་པ་གྱིས་ལ༔ (connective: "…and"); other recension མོས་པ་གྱིས་ཤིག༔ (imperative). Print གཏོད་ལ༔ སྨོན་ལམ་འདི་སྐད་དུ; other recension གཏོད་ལ་སྨོན་ལམ་འདི་སྐད. Same.
- 41.5: print སྨོན་ལམ་དེ་སྐད་དུ་བཏབ་པས ("having made the prayer thus"); other recension སྨོན་ལམ་བཏབ་པས. Same sense.
